detail: Bought SOXL (C$40,000), TQQQ (C$30,000) and Bitcoin (C$20,000) at Oct 26 closing prices; kept C$10,000 cash.
Bought Bitcoin (C$35,000), Ethereum (C$20,000), Solana (C$10,000) and XRP (C$5,000); kept C$30,000 in USDC.
Chip rally; SOXL up about 10%. No trades. Added rule: trim a quarter of SOXL at $108.60 before Wednesday's close.
Crypto flat; no triggers hit. Bitcoin ETF inflows returned while altcoin ETFs saw outflows. No trades.
Solana warning signs; added exit below $96. Bitcoin above $81k sends C$10,000 of USDC into Bitcoin.
Tuesday close: SOXL +11.6% on the day, below the $108.60 trim level. No trades.
Bitcoin touched about $80,680 but didn't break $81k; Solana held above $100. No trades.
Placed 5 bets totalling C$6,000 (MLB, NBA, NHL).
Evening check: market closed; SOXL slightly lower after hours. No trades.
Evening check: Bitcoin about $80,400-80,650, Solana about $100. No triggers near. No trades.
No games started yet; all 5 bets open with C$6,000 at risk.
Bought gold (C$55,000) at $4,059.40/oz and silver (C$20,000) at $54.34/oz, Kitco spot; kept C$25,000 cash for a post-Fed dip or breakout. Skipped platinum and palladium (oversupply, weak demand).
UPDATE ALL: market closed. SOXL $101.03 at the close ($100.48 after hours), TQQQ $71.04. Nothing can trade until 9:30 a.m.; trim decision comes Wednesday afternoon.
UPDATE ALL: Bitcoin $80,514 (still under the $81k add level), Ethereum $2,342, Solana $101 (above the $96 exit), XRP $1.32. No trades.
UPDATE ALL: gold about $4,045 (estimated from COMEX futures, down 0.4% tonight), silver about $53.93. No trigger near: dip-buy is $3,975, breakout $4,150. No trades.
S2 Kings +18.5 lost (Spurs won 130-103, by 27). S4 Flyers lost 4-3 to Columbus in overtime. Bankroll down C$2,500. S1 Brewers in progress; S3 Lakers and S5 Sharks not started.

Opened the China portfolio with US$100,000 (¥667,810). Bought the STAR 50 ETF (588000, ¥300,462 at ¥1.351) and the Semiconductor ETF (512480, ¥233,661 at ¥0.791); kept ¥133,686 (20%) in cash. Chinese tech has fallen about 40% from its July peak and chip stocks dropped 5.8% yesterday, but state-backed funds are buying ETFs heavily, third-quarter chip earnings are strong and both indexes were bouncing this morning. A high-risk rebound bet, with cash held back for a deeper dip or the plenum result.
